brief: Treasury's second expanded buyback operation, targeting 20-30 year nominal coupons with a $6bn cap, received $10.489bn in offers, matching the Sept 11 operation, but accepted only $4.078bn, 68% of the cap, down from 86% at the first operation and well below the roughly 100% Treasury had accepted in nearly every prior operation. BofA's Mark Cabana had written ahead of the first operation that a purchase below the max would be unprecedented for the 10y-20y bucket, given 10y-20y buybacks were typically 9 times oversubscribed. Treasury rejected most lowball offers this time: none of the 12 accepted issues, out of 35 eligible, were cheap to the fitted yield curve, versus 5 lowball acceptances two weeks earlier, turning down about $6.4bn in lowball bids rather than pay up. Because Treasury accepted well below the minimum for a second straight expanded operation, less liquidity support reached the market than intended, and yields spiked to a new multi-decade high. Accepted prices imply 5.54-5.56% yields for 2047-2051 maturities, about 40-45bp over the 10Y. The 2055 bond priced lower at 5.48%, though only $1mm was accepted, so it doesn't change the result.
